Identical to perfect_foresight_weather_lightgbm (same features, model, hyperparameters), but refit 6 times (~4-month windows) on an expanding window instead of once — tests whether that alone narrows offshore wind’s extrapolation ceiling (target is still absolute MW, not rescaled).

Same features and periodic-refit schedule (6 windows) as perfect_foresight_weather_lightgbm_quarterly_refit, CatBoost instead of LightGBM (matching hyperparameters) — general algorithm comparison, not a fix for offshore’s extrapolation ceiling (CatBoost is also tree-based).

Same features and periodic-refit schedule (6 windows) as perfect_foresight_weather_lightgbm_quarterly_refit, XGBoost instead of LightGBM (matching hyperparameters) — general algorithm comparison, not a fix for offshore’s extrapolation ceiling (XGBoost is also tree-based).

LightGBM (300 trees, max_depth=6), identical to baseline_lightgbm plus PECD v4.2 capacity-weighted capacity factor + MaStR installed capacity per technology, both assumed perfectly known at the forecast horizon. pv/wind_onshore/wind_offshore get their own technology’s pair; load gets all three (testing PV self-consumption suppressing grid load) plus PECD 2m temperature at country level.
LightGBM (300 trees, max_depth=6) on the identical feature set as the linear regression baseline. No weather/capacity data.
Linear regression (standardized features) on seasonality (daily/annual) + short lags (1h, 2h, 24h, 48h) + load-only weekday features. No weather/capacity data.
